topic: Kosmos Energy exit and Petrosen takeover (2025-2026)
wiki_text: In late 2025 Kosmos Energy signalled its intention to exit the Yakaar-Teranga project: in a statement dated 11 December 2025 the company said that 'in the absence of a new partner, Kosmos will work with Petrosen to transfer the block back to the Senegalese state on or before the license expiry in July 2026.' On 23 April 2026 Senegalese Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko announced that the government had secured a joint withdrawal agreement of Kosmos Energy and Petrosen from the Cayar offshore (Yakaar-Teranga) license, concluded without financial compensation to the Senegalese state, with the license to be reassigned exclusively to the national company Petrosen subject to validation by ministerial decree. Following the handover, Petrosen assumed full responsibility for advancing the deepwater gas field and now targets a final investment decision in 2026, with first gas expected in the 2028-2029 timeframe. The project remains pre-FID. Recoverable resources are estimated at roughly 20-25 trillion cubic feet, and development cost estimates range from about $3 billion to $7.5 billion.

topic: Start-up of Africa's first LNG-to-power project (2025)
wiki_text: The Karmol Dakar FSRU began commissioning in spring 2025: the FSRU received its first LNG cargo in May 2025, and on 29 April 2025 regasified LNG was transferred from the FSRU to Karpowership's powership KPS 10, achieving power generation. By mid-July 2025 the LNG-to-power project off Dakar was reported as up and running and supplying electricity to Senegal's grid, described as Africa's first LNG-to-power project; together with the earlier Karadeniz Powership Ayşegül Sultan, the Karpowership fleet was reported to supply roughly a quarter of Senegal's electricity. The terminal has a baseload import capacity of 2.5 mtpa.
